title: Scalar extension preserves finite presentations of internal sheaf modules
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $R,S$ be commutative ring objects in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ with its sheaf tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], and let $\varphi\colon R\to S$ be a morphism of ring objects [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. For every finitely presented $R$-module object $M$ [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], the $S$-module object $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}M=S\otimes_R M$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] is finitely presented. More precisely, if $M\cong\operatorname{coker}(f\colon R^m\to R^n)$, there are canonical isomorphisms $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}(R^k)\cong S^k$ for every $k\in\mathbf N$, under which $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}M\cong\operatorname{coker}(f_S\colon S^m\to S^n)$, with $f_S$ the conjugate of $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}(f)$. No flatness of $S$ over $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Final clause: tensoring local finite presentations on the strata gives local finite presentations; finite-free and cokernel calculation

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ and $E=\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$. The abelianness assertion of [lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification], applied to the small pro-étale site with coefficients $\Ab$, makes $\mathcal C$ abelian. By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], both tensor functors preserve colimits; by [lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive] they are additive. In particular $R\otimes-$ and $S\otimes-$ preserve finite colimits, so [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] makes both module categories abelian. The hypotheses of [def-sfb-modobj-extension] hold: the category is symmetric, it has coequalizers, both tensor functors preserve colimits, and $R$ is commutative. Thus $E$ is the stated balanced-tensor functor. By [lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact] it preserves finite colimits; applying [lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive] to these module categories also shows $E(0_{A,B})=0_{E(A),E(B)}$.

source.place: Final clause, verifying the hypotheses for the finite-free and cokernel calculation

proof.text: Give $S$ its left regular $S$-action and its right $R$-action $\rho_S=\mu_S\circ(S\otimes\varphi)$, the mixed bimodule specified in [def-sfb-modobj-extension]. Its tensor product with the regular $R$-bimodule is precisely the coequalizer defining $E(R)$. Apply [lem-sfb-mixed-bimodule-right-unitor] to this $S$-$R$-bimodule and forget the right action. This gives the canonical $S$-linear isomorphism $e_1:E(R)\xrightarrow{\sim}S$. If $q:S\otimes R\to E(R)$ is the quotient, its normalization is $e_1\circ q=\mu_S\circ(S\otimes\varphi)$; its inverse is $q\circ(S\otimes\eta_R)\circ(\rho_S^{\mathcal C})^{-1}$, where $\rho_S^{\mathcal C}:S\otimes\mathbf1\cong S$ is the ambient right unitor. The mixed-bimodule theorem supplies $S$-linearity as well as invertibility, so no identification of $R$ with $S$ or flatness is being used.

source.place: Final clause, the rank-one balanced-tensor comparison

proof.text: For $k\geq0$ use the finite biproducts $R^k,S^k$ of [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], viewed as finite coproducts. By [lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact], the maps $E(\iota_i^R):E(R)\to E(R^k)$ exhibit $E(R^k)$ as the coproduct of $k$ copies of $E(R)$. Consequently there is a unique $e_k:E(R^k)\to S^k$ with $e_k\circ E(\iota_i^R)=\iota_i^S\circ e_1$, and a unique $d_k:S^k\to E(R^k)$ with $d_k\circ\iota_i^S=E(\iota_i^R)\circ e_1^{-1}$. Their composites are identities: precompose with each coproduct injection and use $e_1e_1^{-1}=1$ and $e_1^{-1}e_1=1$; uniqueness of coproduct maps gives the equalities. Thus $e_k$ is a canonical isomorphism with inverse $d_k$. For $k=0$ the same argument is the uniqueness of maps between initial objects, giving $E(0)\cong0$.

source.place: Final clause, finite-free comparison in every rank including zero

proof.text: Fix a presentation $M\cong Q=\operatorname{coker}(f:R^m\to R^n)$ as in [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], with cokernel arrow $q_f:R^n\to Q$. A cokernel is the coequalizer of $(f,0)$: both universal properties say that maps out of $R^n$ killing $f$ factor uniquely through $q_f$. Since $E$ preserves finite colimits [lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact] and preserves zero morphisms by step 1, $E(q_f)$ is a cokernel of $E(f)$. Set $f_S=e_n\circ E(f)\circ e_m^{-1}$ and $q_S=E(q_f)\circ e_n^{-1}:S^n\to E(Q)$. Then $q_Sf_S=0$. For any $S$-linear $h:S^n\to N$ with $hf_S=0$, the map $h e_n$ kills $E(f)$, since $e_n E(f)=f_S e_m$. There is therefore a unique $u:E(Q)\to N$ with $u E(q_f)=h e_n$; equivalently $u q_S=h$. This proves that $q_S$ is a cokernel of $f_S$. Applying the two cokernel universal properties gives inverse maps $E(Q)\cong\operatorname{coker}(f_S)$ characterized by the cokernel arrows, so the comparison is canonical. Finally applying the functor $E$ to the given isomorphism $M\cong Q$ gives $E(M)\cong\operatorname{coker}(f_S)$.

source.place: Final clause, preserving the cokernel and writing out the conjugated presentation

proof.text: The integers $m,n$ in step 4 are finite and its arrow $f_S:S^m\to S^n$ is $S$-linear. Hence the displayed isomorphism is exactly a witness to finite presentation over $S$ by [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. All steps used finite colimits and the mixed right unitor; none required scalar extension to preserve kernels, so no flatness hypothesis was needed.

source.place: Final clause, finite presentation of the extended module

Step 1: the hypotheses hold. sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor gives colimit preservation of F⊗– and –⊗F for every F, so lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive gives additivity. Then lem-sfb-modobj-abelian makes both module categories abelian, def-sfb-modobj-extension applies (braided, R commutative), and lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact makes E right exact. E(0)=0 because E is additive. Step 2: with P=S, the coequaliser in lem-sfb-mixed-bimodule-right-unitor is the same pair, with the same bracketing (μ_S(S⊗φ))⊗R and (S⊗μ_R)α, as the one defining E(R). So e_1 is an S-linear iso with e_1q=μ_S(S⊗φ), and S≠R is allowed. Step 3: the finite coproduct comparison is correctly elementary, including k=0. Step 4: E(q_f) is the cokernel of the conjugate f_S, with existence and uniqueness checked. Step 5: (m,n,f_S) is exactly a witness for def-sfb-finitely-presented-module. Edge cases tested: m=0, n=0, φ=id, S=0, X=∅, and the non-flat map ℤ→ℤ/2 (only right exactness is used). review_split passes, and the two tool_uses (grothendieck-sheafification, modobj-abelian) are only ambient abelianness, which I accept.
